title: Sealed peer channel: identity-keyed members across NAT through one hub port
goal: Every byte between Susi machines travels inside a sealed peer channel built on the crypto core already links (X25519, ChaCha20-Poly1305, SHA-256, Ed25519 node identities): Noise XXpsk0 with the node keys as static keys and the cluster key as PSK, per hop (link) and end to end (call). A hub listens on one dedicated, configurable channel port (peer_channel_listen, default 29090, never the 9090-9095 block); members behind NAT dial out, keep a persistent uplink with keepalive and reconnect, and are called over it; member-to-member calls are relayed by the hub as end-to-end ciphertext it cannot open. Membership is identity-keyed (signed requests verify by node key, not source address; the channel admits by proven identity), remote plaintext on the contract ports is refused unconditionally (allow_remote_plaintext retired with a one-time notice), UDP discovery answers the local network only, and the threat model and docs/peer-channel.md describe the construction, the topology, the forwarded port and firewall rule, and the upgrade path.
acceptance: cargo test -p susi --test peer_channel_hub --offline --locked passes: a hub and two members in isolated homes on offsets of 500 and up, members connecting only outbound through a recording forwarder; member-to-hub, member-to-member (relayed) and hub-to-member MCP initialize calls succeed with every roster advertising addresses the traffic never comes from; plaintext HTTP on the channel port, a replayed handshake, a wrong identity, a node without the cluster key, an impostor of a member's node id and an unbound identity asking for a relay are refused; the forwarder capture and the hub's relay trace show no request line, header, JSON or node id.
